cells.tense: You can feel the pull of what might be and stay steady inside it.
cells.ask: Choose one possibility you have been carrying quietly and say one plain sentence about it to the person it concerns.
cells.core:
You can hold a lot of what might be felt and still be standing in it. The pull is real and you are not run by it — you feel what's between you two and you keep your own shape. That is the part people rarely manage: staying warm while staying whole.

What makes it work is that you're not cataloguing the feelings. You're seeing the shape of them, which one belongs to you and which one belongs to the other person. That pattern-reading is your quiet gift here — it keeps the connection honest. This balance is a seed and seeds are free to grow, though keeping them open costs something. Say the one thing out loud today; the pull already did its part.

cells.tense: You will pour the whole harvest at someone before they have asked for any of it.
cells.ask: Pick one person and one evening this week, and let the first move belong to them.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of a moment that hasn't arrived. Before anyone has asked, you feel the many possible ways this could go — and you gather them all, offering the whole bundle at once so nothing can slip past. The pull is doing its work too early, and the other person is getting a briefing instead of a conversation.

The connection you want is built on what's actually here, not on everything that might be. The feeling is real; the timing is off. Holding all of it steady until it's wanted costs you something, and paying that cost is not the same as being generous. Leave the first move to them this week and let what's actually there have room to show up.

cells.tense: You knew how to reach toward people once, and you have been standing back from it since.
cells.ask: Reach out to one person you have been leaving alone, without asking anything from them in return.
cells.core:
You feel someone across from you and let them stay a separate person. You notice what they might be feeling, and you don't need it to be about you. No fusing, no distance — two people, warm, present, each still whole. That's the whole of it, and it's ordinary enough that it can go unnoticed.

The feeling is there and the acting on it isn't. You sense the connection you'd like and you stay put. People around you may not know it's available. The feeling hasn't gone anywhere; the step from feeling to showing is what stopped. One hand reaching this week, asking nothing back, is enough to start it moving.

cells.tense: You are already pulling people toward what might be felt, and you describe it as though it were happening to you.
cells.ask: Say the word 'I' in front of one thing you noticed yourself doing toward someone this week.
cells.core:
You're already gathering the possibilities between you and other people — the way you hold a room, the way you leave a door open in a conversation, the way someone leaves lighter. It's happening. And you explain it as the mood passing through, or the other person's doing, or just how things went.

The pen is in your hand and you're describing it as something else. There's small relief in that, and a cost: you can't trust a gift you won't name as yours. Notice that your pull is a pattern, not an accident, and claim one instance of it out loud this week.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person has actually gathered several people or options; it describes a capacity for pulling many possible feelings toward them, so anything about the size of their social supply is inference. A reader could say the choosing is not theirs to make, because someone else held the pen; I will keep the claims on what they are doing rather than on what was done to them. The asks survive being wrong: each is a small public action that teaches something about their own pull even if the read missed, and they do not make anything contingent on the reading being true. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about 'the abundance,' since it flatters the card instead of the life — I am cutting it.
